verdict: The revision fixes the prior root-level synthesis, misplaced access-control hierarchy, runtime split, and overbroad prerequisites, and it gives all eight discovery tasks a plausible home. It is close to a usable training plan, but one observed task is still deliberately anchored in two sibling sections and two broadened leaves combine capabilities whose probes do not predict one another, so leaf-level sampling and mapping are not yet fully stable.
findings: Coverage: All six C03 guideposts remain covered, and the eight discovery tasks have concrete homes: unix-001 in c03.shell-data-semantics, unix-002 in c03.package-lifecycle, unix-003 in c03.file-record-transforms or c03.shell-data-semantics depending on the unresolved boundary, unix-004 in c03.persistent-service-operation, unix-005 in c03.process-lifecycle-resources, unix-006 in c03.route-selection, unix-007 in c03.system-time, and unix-008 in c03.operational-streams-logs. The revision also supplies the previously weak CPU, memory, and descriptor diagnosis plus credential lifecycle and delegated-command coverage. Firewall administration is only mentioned as diagnostic evidence and not trained as a configuration outcome, but neither the guideposts nor the supplied routing task makes that omission blocking.

Observable outcomes: Outcomes consistently name an operation and a checkable result. In particular, the six roots no longer describe loose unions: reliable shell automation requires boundary preservation, transformation, and failure control in one job; runtime provisioning combines package provenance with scoped environment and time behavior; service incident control combines process, log, and manager evidence; host access combines resource permissions with authentication or delegation; network connectivity combines path and endpoint evidence; and storage recoverability combines live storage work with a proved recovery point.

Boundaries: The earlier shell-redirection versus operational-log overlap is fixed, and host identity work is now cleanly separated from network reachability. A concrete sibling ambiguity remains for unix-003. c03.file-record-transforms uses almost that exact filename-derivation task as a probe, while c03.shell-data-semantics also uses a loop that splits stored filenames and expands glob characters; its excludes only rule out file-content parsing, not filename decomposition. State that diagnosing expansion, splitting, or array-to-argument formation belongs to shell-data-semantics, whereas deriving and validating the new filename mapping belongs to file-record-transforms, and revise one probe so the same task is not a positive anchor for both.

Learnable progression: Removing all three broad prerequisites from v1 is justified: the supplied tasks do not establish that runtime context requires shell-state mastery, backup design requires the complete filesystem-operations outcome, or service configuration requires full process and log diagnosis. Each root's two probes now require evidence from every child rather than sampling one child alone, so the internal nodes train real synthesis. No missing prerequisite is demonstrated by the supplied tasks.

Useful granularity: Most leaves support varied tasks with a shared decision or correctness contract, and splitting runtime context into process environment and system time was warranted. c03.process-lifecycle-resources remains too heterogeneous: unix-005 and the first probe require signal and deadline semantics, while the second probe requires CPU, memory, and descriptor attribution; success on either is weak evidence for the other. c03.authentication-privilege has the same smaller problem: fixed-command and environment-safe delegation in its first probe does not predict key lifecycle, emergency access, and login revocation in its second. Split these pairs if both distributions will be sampled, or narrow each outcome and its probes to a single predictive capability rather than retaining coverage through a compound leaf.

Generation probe: Every section has two executable, substantively different instructions. All root pairs pass the cross-child synthesis test, including both storage tasks requiring a restorable copy around a filesystem change and both access tasks requiring file policy plus an authentication or privilege boundary. The weak probes are at the two compound leaves: the process pair divides timing from resource diagnosis, and the authentication-privilege pair divides delegated execution from credential administration instead of demonstrating variants of one outcome.

Mapping: No held-out retrieval results were supplied, so mapping quality cannot be scored empirically. Seven discovery tasks have a clear primary leaf. unix-003 is a reproducible expected instability because two sibling anchors both closely paraphrase it; this is a curriculum boundary error, not a case for a source-specific mapping rule. unix-005 remains primarily process-lifecycle-resources rather than shell-execution-control because its decisive knowledge is process-wide signal interruption and deadline handling in threaded code, not shell control flow.

Size: Twenty-one sections at depth two are still manageable, and unlike v1 the six roots add distinct cross-child task distributions rather than duplicating their leaves. The extra system-time and host-access distinctions change generation and evaluation in useful ways. c03.name-endpoint-diagnosis is the least evidenced addition: the inventory has no network guidepost and the sole network discovery task exercises route policy, not DNS or listening endpoints. Retain it only if broader held-out tasks support that distribution; otherwise collapse the network branch to one route-and-path capability. Any split of the two compound leaves should be offset by removing such weakly evidenced expansion rather than growing the taxonomy automatically.
